st: Use kitchen scissors to cut down the top of each lobster shell, stopping at the tail fin. Loosen the meat slightly, keeping it in the shell. Pat dry.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the shallot and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lobster tails meat-side down and cook for 3 minutes. Flip and cook 5 more minutes, until the meat is opaque and reaches 140°F (60°C). Remove to a plate.
Add the vanilla seeds and the empty pod to the same pan with the cream.
Simmer the cream gently until it reduces slightly and coats a spoon.
Stir in the lime juice, the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter, salt and pepper. Remove the vanilla pod.
Return the lobster to the pan and spoon the sauce over it for 1 minute to reheat.
Serve with rice and lime wedges.

ing: firm, such as snapper, cut in chunks
st: Rinse the cassava leaves and drain them. They must always be cooked well, never eaten raw.
Put the leaves in a pot with [[3 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low until the leaves are very soft and darker.
Drain extra water if the pot is very wet, then mash or blend the leaves coarsely.
In a separate pan, heat the oil and cook the onion until golden, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the onion mixture and salt to the cassava leaves.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer, stirring, for 15 minutes.
Add the fish chunks, cover and cook gently until opaque and flaky.
Serve hot with rice or boiled green bananas.
Put the beef in a pot with [[3 cups]] water, half the garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer covered until tender. Strain, saving the broth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the onions and cook until deep golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Add the remaining garlic and the beef and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and stir to coat for 2 minutes.
Pour in [[4 cups]] hot beef broth (top up with water if needed) and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, reduce the heat to low and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone.
Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork before serving.

ing: peeled, cut into chunks; or plantains
st: Rub the peeled bananas with a little oil to stop sticking. Boil them in [[2 cups]] salted water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Rub the fish with the lime juice and half the salt. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they soften into a sauce, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and remaining salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the bananas and simmer for 10 minutes.
Nestle in the fish. Cover and cook gently until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Serve hot straight from the pot.
Warm the coconut milk until just lukewarm. Stir in the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar and rest for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the yeast mixture and mix, adding up to [[0.25 cup]] warm water, to make a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled.
Heat a heavy skillet over medium-low heat and brush with oil.
Scoop about [[0.5 cup]] dough into the pan and spread it into a round about half an inch thick. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Cover and cook until the bottom is golden and the top looks set, then flip and cook the other side, about 10 minutes total.
Repeat with the rest of the dough. Serve warm with tea or stew.
Toast the rice flour in a dry skillet over low heat, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and turns very pale gold, about 8 minutes. Do not let it brown.
Pour the flour into a large bowl and cool for 5 minutes.
Grind the peanuts in a food processor until fine, but stop before they turn into butter.
Add the peanuts, sugar and cardamom to the bowl and mix.
Pour in the melted ghee and mix with your hands.
Add the warm milk a spoonful at a time until the mix holds together when squeezed.
Roll the mixture into balls about the size of a walnut.
Let them set for 15 minutes before serving. Store in an airtight container.
